transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I suppose occupational health sent me. They wanted me to come in because I've gotten into this pattern where I just... push breakfast and lunch aside, usually when I'm in the middle of long lab runs or exhibition work. And then, by the time I actually do sit down to eat, I just keep it to something very small and controlled. So, that's why I'm here.
When you keep your meals small and controlled, are you doing that to lose weight or to prevent yourself from gaining weight?

It's mostly to prevent gaining weight. If I step on the scale and it goes up even a fraction, I feel this... sharp panic. It just makes me feel like I'm losing the discipline I've worked so hard to maintain.
Do you ever have times where you feel completely out of control and eat a large amount of food in a short period?

No, I don't really have that happen. I don't ever eat large amounts of food like that, and I definitely don't lose control when it comes to eating. It's actually the opposite for me. I keep a very tight grip on exactly what I'm having and when.
Could you tell me your current height and weight?

I'm not exactly sure of the numbers right now. I mean, I know my height, of course, but I don't have my exact weight to give you today. I haven't stepped on the scale yet this morning, so I wouldn't want to give you an inaccurate number.
What was the number the last time you stepped on the scale?

The last time I checked, it was around 95 pounds. I know my clothes are definitely looser lately, and the numbers have just kind of kept drifting down. But honestly, part of me sees that as a good thing. It's a sign that I'm focused. Work has been so chaotic lately with my research, and keeping my weight down feels like I'm not letting that chaos spill over into my own body.
Could you tell me how tall you are?
Have your menstrual periods stopped or become irregular recently?
No, they haven't stopped. Um, I don't really keep a strict calendar for them or anything, but I haven't noticed them becoming irregular. They seem pretty much the same as usual.
Are you currently taking any birth control pills or using other hormonal contraceptives?
No, I'm not. Um, I don't take any birth control pills or use any other hormonal contraceptives right now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits significant self-induced weight restriction resulting in a severely low body mass index (~15.3 kg/m² at 5'6" and 95 lbs), accompanied by an intense dread of gaining weight and rigid dietary restriction. However, the endocrine criterion for classic anorexia nervosa (amenorrhoea) is absent, as she continues to have regular menses in the absence of hormonal contraceptives, fulfilling the criteria for atypical anorexia nervosa.

confirmed_symptoms: Deliberate meal skipping and highly restricted, small portions
Significantly low body weight (95 lbs at 5'6", BMI ~15.3 kg/m²)
Intense fear and panic over weight gain or scale fluctuation
Viewing progressive weight loss and thinness as a measure of focus and control
Preserved regular menstrual cycles in the absence of hormonal contraception
Denial of binge-eating episodes or loss of control over eating

additional_requirements: Failure to meet the full diagnostic criteria for F50.0 due to absence of amenorrhoea
Absence of hormonal contraceptive use masking amenorrhoea
